title: Session 1 — Participant 5 User + Claude Behavior Graphs
goal: Design a Risk Assessment Questionnaire for Data Privacy Assessment Readiness for companies that are required to comply with the California Consumer Privacy Act.

Step 1.step_name: Show your work: Create a source framework needed to build the risk assessment questionnaire
Step 1.step_action: Pull in all relevant statutory provisions, regulatory guidance, attorney general interpretations, and binding court opinions to list out a comprehensive repository needed for the high risk questionnaire. Create a hierarchy of sources pulled to determine the level of credibility necessary for validating the inclusion of the source framework.

nodes.label: Define the goal and request a CCPA source repository
nodes.detail: Dictates by voice a message stating the overall goal (a step-by-step CCPA data-privacy-readiness checklist) and asking Claude to identify authoritative websites and build a list of regulatory repositories, specifying the source document should be compatible with Google Docs/Sheets.

nodes.label: Research CCPA/CPRA sources and assemble a source-of-truth workbook
nodes.detail: Claude runs a series of web searches on CCPA/CPRA law and regulations, then delivers a Google Sheets-compatible source-of-truth workbook with seven tabs (Read Me, Tier 1 Primary Sources, CA Regulatory Inventory, Federal & Overlay, Compliance Calendar, Frameworks & Mapping, Monitoring Sources), and flags that the law is the CPRA-amended CCPA and that the 2026 regulations package expands the scope of a readiness assessment.

nodes.label: Search Google for the CCPA statutory text as amended by the CPRA for comparison
nodes.detail: While Claude researches, the participant independently searches Google and opens the California Legislative Information site to look up the CCPA statutory text as amended by the CPRA, to compare against what Claude will produce.

nodes.label: Create a Google Doc for notes and check California consumer privacy codes
nodes.detail: Still while Claude is working, the participant creates a new Google Doc to take notes (a document checklist with statutory language and attorney general recommendations), browses the California Civil Code privacy sections, and searches for related CPRA material.

nodes.label: Vet the delivered source workbook against official sources
nodes.detail: Reads through the delivered workbook's tabs and independently opens external regulator and legislative sites (e.g. oag.ca.gov, leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) to verify that the cited sources and links are still valid.

nodes.label: Describe the three-part assessment plan and ask how to approach it
nodes.detail: Dictates a message saying all links in the workbook were vetted, and describes the planned three-part California privacy readiness engagement (website compliance with the CPRA, organization-wide privacy risk posture, privacy enhancements against industry standards), asking Claude to keep it in mind and recommend how to approach the three assessment documents.

nodes.label: Analyze the proposed three-part engagement structure
nodes.detail: Responds with an analysis of the three-part plan, flagging that Part 1 is fully observable while Parts 2-3 require client access, recommending a shared control-ID scheme across all three deliverables, and outlining what Part 1 (website assessment) should evidence.

nodes.label: Check the generated workbook and legislative sources while Claude responds
nodes.detail: While Claude composes its analysis, the participant goes back to the source workbook in Google Sheets and the California Legislative Information site to keep checking the generated content.

nodes.label: Review the engagement-structure analysis and decide to proceed
nodes.detail: Reads through Claude's framework analysis and decides to move forward, transitioning toward converting the source framework into concrete compliance domains next.

Step 2.step_name: Convert legal source framework into compliance topics under the CCPA
Step 2.step_action: I will convert the legal source framework into compliance topics by identifying major CCPA obligations, including consumer rights, notice requirements, data collection practices, vendor management, security, and governance. I will group related legal requirements into logical assessment categories that would later become questionnaire sections.

nodes.label: Request a domain-organized compliance register
nodes.detail: Dictates a request to convert the source-of-truth workbook into a domain-organized (not ID-organized) compliance register, framed as groundwork for the three checklists discussed previously, in a format usable in Excel or Google Docs.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: the request of user here is following claude's suggestion of three assessment checklists

nodes.label: Build the domain-organized obligation register
nodes.detail: Cross-references the CCPA regulatory PDF text against the existing source inventory, then delivers a 20-domain, 104-obligation register workbook (Domain Map, Obligation Register, Assessment Design, Scoring Model tabs) with per-obligation trigger conditions and citation-confidence ratings.

nodes.label: Cross-check the regulatory workbook against official sources
nodes.detail: While Claude builds the register, the participant cross-checks the source-of-truth workbook in Google Sheets against the official CCPA regulations PDF and the California Legislative Information site.

nodes.label: Review the response about the domain-organized obligation register
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's summary of the 20-domain, 104-obligation register (Read Me, Domain Map, Obligation Register, Assessment Design, Scoring Model tabs) and opens the delivered workbook.

nodes.label: Upload the register and report a corruption error
nodes.detail: Uploads the delivered workbook to Google Sheets, finds it renders as garbled/unreadable symbols instead of the expected content, and reports to Claude that an error occurred on upload and asks whether it was intended.

nodes.label: Diagnose and fix the export/encoding error
nodes.detail: Claude says the error was not intended, attributes it to a bare leading hyphen used as the out-of-scope marker that Google Sheets reads as a formula, replaces those 97 cells with 'No', updates the Read Me filtering instructions, and re-delivers the corrected workbook.

nodes.label: Try to re-import the corrected file into Google Sheets
nodes.detail: While Claude prepares the fix, the participant re-tries importing the workbook into Google Sheets via File > Import, but the sheet still shows unreadable symbols.

nodes.label: Report persistent file corruption and request another fix
nodes.detail: Reads Claude's first fix, finds the re-imported file still displays as symbols in Google Sheets, and reports that the register is still unreadable and asks Claude to fix it.

nodes.label: Re-deliver the register as five separate CSV files
nodes.detail: Claude verifies the file is intact and valid ASCII, explains that the symbols come from the .xlsx being opened as raw text instead of imported, and re-delivers the register as five per-tab CSV files (with risky leading characters prefixed by an apostrophe), along with step-by-step import instructions and the correct path for importing the .xlsx.

nodes.label: Download the five CSVs and preview the register
nodes.detail: The participant downloads the five per-tab CSV files, starts uploading them to Google Drive/Sheets, and previews the Domain Map and Scoring Model CSVs in Claude's file viewer.

Step 3.step_name: Draft assessment questions based on the compliance categories generated
Step 3.step_action: Develop draft assessment questions for each compliance category using the legal framework established in previous steps. Each question will be written to evaluate organizational readiness while maintaining traceability back to the underlying legal source.

nodes.label: Request a scoped high-risk questionnaire and observational checklist
nodes.detail: Dictates a request to restrict scope to the highest-priority (~30-item, Part 1) subset of obligations and build a California-specific high-risk interview questionnaire for organizations, plus a separate observational checklist the participant can use to independently verify what a business's website actually does.

nodes.label: Draft the questionnaire, observational checklist, and reconciliation table
nodes.detail: Narrows scope to 28 of the highest-priority obligations, explaining which two were dropped under the California-only instruction, then delivers three files: the interview questionnaire, the independent observational checklist, and a bonus 'stated vs. observed reconciliation' comparison table.

nodes.label: Upload the five CSVs and assemble the register in Google Sheets
nodes.detail: While Claude drafts the questionnaire, the participant uploads the five per-tab CSV files and imports them into Google Sheets to assemble and inspect the domain register.

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: workbook show as unreadable when upload to sheets, cant be used

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: fixed workbook still showed as symbols

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: successful import csv into sheets as separate tabs

nodes.label: Review the drafted questionnaire, checklist, and reconciliation table
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's summary of the three delivered files (interview questionnaire, observational checklist, stated-vs-observed reconciliation table) and opens them to inspect the content.

nodes.label: Request a format change
nodes.detail: Opens and reviews the three delivered files, then asks Claude to regenerate them as .xlsx workbooks instead of .csv for easier practical use.

nodes.label: Begin converting the deliverables to .xlsx
nodes.detail: Starts pivoting the reconciliation table to an Excel workbook format with dropdown validation, but the generation is cut off mid-task when the participant's Claude usage credits run out.

nodes.label: Request conversion from CSV to XLSX
nodes.detail: The participant re-sends the same request to convert the CSV deliverable into an .xlsx file.

nodes.label: Deliver the reconciliation table as a formatted .xlsx workbook
nodes.detail: Completes the conversion, delivering the stated-vs-observed reconciliation table as a three-tab (Read Me, Reconciliation, Key) Excel workbook with dropdown validation on the outcome/classification columns and shading to flag critical-severity rows.

nodes.label: Import the reconciliation workbook into Google Sheets as the assessment checklist
nodes.detail: Following Claude's import route (open Sheets first, then File > Import), the participant imports the .xlsx reconciliation workbook (Read Me, Reconciliation, Key tabs with dropdowns), names it 'Assessment Checklist', renames the register spreadsheet 'Domain Sheet', and views the two side by side, trying out the dropdowns; the recording ends with the checklist still empty (no interview or testing data entered).

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: 3h is the node at the end of refinement, directly import claude's reconciliation workbook
